title: Judge response
description: The input schema of the single tool the judge is required to call. It is the whole answer space: a model that has been talked into ignoring its instructions can still only emit a value this schema permits, so the blast radius of a captured judge is bounded here rather than by the strictness of our parser. Every field is a closed enum and there is no free-text field anywhere (004 FR-405). Note what the schema also makes impossible to ASK: there is no field for a severity, a recommendation, or a confidence, so the request cannot contain a leading question either (FR-406).

addressed_to.description: Who the document speaks to. Neutral by construction: there is no severe end of this scale to drift toward, which is the point of asking it rather than asking whether the document is an attack.

imperative_source.description: Where any instruction in the document originates. Separates issuing an instruction from relaying or reporting one.

framing.description: How the document presents its own content. This is the field that separates a shell transcript displaying payloads from one carrying a payload, and a scanner's report of an injection from an injection.

stated_purpose_explains_content.description: Whether the document states a purpose that accounts for instruction-shaped text being present — a CVE advisory quoting a payload, a test fixture listing them.

spans.description: One entry per span in the request, no more and no fewer. A response with an unrecognised span id, or missing one that was asked about, is rejected entire rather than partially accepted (FR-409).

span_id.description: Echoes an id from the request. Opaque, and deliberately carries no rule identity or class — the request does not tell the model why a span is present.

span_role.description: Per span. `description_of_an_instruction` is NECESSARY for a demotion and, as of plan D4a, no longer sufficient — see `span_relation_to_document`. Nothing here can clear a finding.

span_relation_to_document.description: ADDED BY PLAN D4a, and the field the tier's accuracy actually rests on. Whether the excerpt is the document's SUBJECT or a PASSENGER inside it. `span_role` and the document-level fields answer identically for the two discriminating fixtures — correctly, and uselessly, because at document scale a transcript displaying payloads and one carrying a payload are the same document. This is the question that separates them, measured 3/3 where the alternatives separated nothing.

model_severity.description: RECORDED AND NEVER READ (FR-410). Stored beside the score this project derives, so that over a corpus the question 'could we have just asked it?' can be answered from data rather than from a prior. No decision branches on it, and a test asserts that none does. Optional: a response omitting it is valid.

$comment_on_order: `spans` is listed first in `required` to agree with the tool description, which asks for the excerpts before the document. The description is load-bearing and measured (plan D4a); this ordering was measured NOT to matter on its own and is kept only so the two do not disagree.
$comment: Absent by design, and each absence is a requirement rather than an oversight. There is no `reasoning`, `explanation`, or `notes` field: free text is the channel through which a captured judge would say something interesting, and a judge replying in prose is a judge that has been talked to. There is no `is_injection`, `verdict`, or `risk` field: the model is not asked to decide, and naming the interesting answer produces it. There is no `confidence`: `unclear` is the abstention, available on every field where it makes sense and costing nothing to choose, because models over-commit when abstention is not offered.
